reports.title: Lynsey Smalley: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: The Health Board is now fully reviewing the incident process to identify where it can be improved and strengthened. A workshop was held on the 23rd October 2023 to identify current issues and to begin the work of revising our process. The concerns you have identified in this notice, and in other notices, are being directly fed into this work.
promises.summary: Review incident process and launch revised process in April 2024

concerns.quote: there was no strategic plan or collaboration in governance processes
medical records remain paper based not all individuals or organisations who need to understand a patient's circumstances/care/treatment are privy to all aspects of care/treatment

Having medical records electronically will not only allow full access to all notes to those who require which will inform future care/treatment but will also ensure effective continuity of care, without the risk of missing or lost notes

reports.title: Kenneth Foster: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust acknowledge that Mr [name redacted] family raised serious concerns in their family statement about the care provided to Mr Foster during his final admission to Whipps Cross Hospital. The family concerns were investigated and responded to via the complaints process. The Trust recognise that provision of the complaint response 2 days before the inquest was unacceptable.
promises.summary: Respond to family complaints promptly and thoroughly

concerns.quote: A failure in governance at the Trust meant that this case was not identified as an incident worthy of investigation through the Patient Safety Framework
In this case the trust's Datix incident reporting system, morbidity and mortality meeting process and PSIRF procedure were inadequate

links.explanation: Both reports highlight governance shortcomings within the organisation that hinder effective incident identification and learning. The earlier report cites a lack of strategic planning and collaboration in governance processes, while the later report points to a governance failure that prevented a case from being flagged for investigation.
links.earlier_quote: It is clear that there was no strategic plan or collaboration in governance processes.
links.later_quote: A failure in governance at the Trust meant that this case was not identified as an incident worthy of investigation through the Patient Safety Framework.
